- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to recent peak.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–5% above recent high or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model may lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates; apply 0.5–1.5% downward correction if price has not moved recently.
- Forecast horizon >14 days: reduce forecast sensitivity to recent sentiment spikes; use sentiment average over last 7 days as anchor.
